title: Microsoft Purview Insider Risk Management: cloud storage, cloud service and Microsoft Fabric indicators as Data leaks policy triggers
summary: The briefing passes: the roadmap facts, opt-in configuration, licensing and processing-unit meter are supported. Minor corrections should complete several navigation paths and clarify that Usage center is in preview and is not in the controls table.

claims.claim: Cloud storage apps (Box, Dropbox, Google Drive), cloud services (Azure, AWS), and Fabric (Power BI, Lakehouse) indicators are supported as Data leaks policy triggers.
claims.quote: With this update, the indicators belonging to cloud storage apps (Box, Dropbox, Google Drive), cloud services (Azure, Amazon Web Services) and Microsoft Fabric (Power BI, Lakehouse) will be supported as triggers in Data leaks policy.

claims.claim: Box, Dropbox, Google Drive, AWS, Azure and Microsoft Fabric (Power BI) indicators are billed on data security processing units.
claims.quote: Insider Risk Management indicators that detect activity in cloud storage apps (Box, Dropbox, Google Drive), cloud services (AWS, Azure), and Microsoft Fabric (Power BI) are billed on data security processing units.

claims.claim: Insider Risk Management processing units are measured daily.
claims.quote: | Insider Risk Management | Detect risky behavior for non-Microsoft 365 locations when using Cloud and generative AI policy indicators | Data Security processing unit as measured on a daily basis |

claims.where: Why it matters; Cost and licensing; rationale: cost
claims.claim: One Insider Risk Management processing unit represents the compute required to process 10,000 user activities.
claims.quote: For Insider Risk Management, a processing unit represents the compute required to process 10,000 such user activities. Billing is based on the number of processing units utilized.

claims.where: Cost and licensing; Scope; controls[2].note; rationale: cost
claims.claim: Pay-as-you-go charges use the Azure subscription associated with Purview.
claims.quote: In this procedure, you enable the Microsoft Purview pay-as-you-go features by associating your Microsoft 365 tenant with an Azure subscription for billing purposes.

claims.claim: Consumption and billing information appears in the Azure portal under Cost Management + Billing.
claims.quote: All consumption and billing information is available in the Azure portal under Cost Management + Billing.

claims.claim: The billing models page points to the Azure pricing page for rates.
claims.quote:
Understand pricing and estimate your expected monthly costs for pay-as-you-go capabilities:

- Microsoft pay-as-you-go pricing

claims.claim: A triggering event determines when a user becomes active in a policy for risk scoring.
claims.quote: Triggering events: Events that determine if a user is active in an Insider Risk Management policy.

claims.claim: Policy indicators determine the risk score for an in-scope user after activation.
claims.quote: Policy indicators: Indicators included in Insider Risk Management policies determine a risk score for an in-scope user. You enable policy indicators from indicators defined in global settings. The policy indicators activate only after a triggering event occurs for a user.

claims.claim: Learn documents cloud storage, cloud service and Microsoft Fabric indicators as built-in policy indicators.
claims.quote:
Built-in indicators

Insider Risk Management includes the following built-in indicators.

claims.claim: Cloud storage indicators detect discovery in Google Drive, Box and Dropbox.
claims.quote:
Use cloud storage indicators to detect the following activities in Google Drive, Box, and Dropbox:

- Discovery: Techniques used to figure out the environment

claims.claim: Cloud storage indicators detect collection in Google Drive, Box and Dropbox.
claims.quote: Collection: Techniques used to gather data of interest

claims.claim: Cloud storage indicators detect exfiltration in Google Drive, Box and Dropbox.
claims.quote: Exfiltration: Techniques used to steal data, such as sensitive documents

claims.claim: Cloud storage indicators detect deletion in Google Drive, Box and Dropbox.
claims.quote: Deletion (impact): Techniques used to disrupt the availability or compromise the integrity of a system

claims.claim: Cloud service indicators cover Amazon S3 and Azure SQL Server and Storage.
claims.quote: These indicators include policy indicators for Amazon S3 and Azure (SQL Server and Storage) that you can use to detect techniques used to avoid detection or risky activities.

claims.claim: Cloud service indicators include disabling trace logs.
claims.quote: Disabling trace logs

claims.claim: Cloud service indicators include changes to SQL Server firewall rules.
claims.quote: Updating or deleting SQL Server firewall rules

claims.claim: Fabric indicators cover viewing Power BI reports.
claims.quote: Figure out the environment (for example, viewing Power BI reports and dashboards).

claims.claim: Fabric indicators cover downloading Power BI reports.
claims.quote: Gather data of interest (for example, downloading Power BI reports).

claims.claim: Fabric indicators cover downgrading or removing sensitivity labels on Power BI or Lakehouse assets.
claims.quote: Obfuscate the data gathered or change protection (for example, downgrading or removing sensitivity labels of Power BI or Lakehouse assets).

claims.claim: Fabric indicators cover sharing Lakehouse data outside the organisation.
claims.quote: Exfiltrate the data (for example, sharing Lakehouse data with people outside the organization).

claims.quote: If you select the Data leaks or Data leaks by priority users templates, you see options on the Triggers for this policy page for custom-triggering events and policy indicators.

claims.claim: Indicators not enabled for the organisation cannot be selected until enabled.
claims.quote: If you're unable to select a listed indicator or sequence, it's because they aren't currently enabled for your organization. To make them available to select and assign to the policy, select the Turn on indicators prompt.

claims.claim: A policy does not evaluate a user without a triggering event unless an administrator manually adds the user in the Users dashboard.
claims.quote: If you add a user to an Insider Risk Management policy but the user doesn't have a triggering event, the policy doesn't evaluate the user's activity unless you manually add the user in the Users dashboard.

claims.claim: A high-severity DLP alert in Exchange, SharePoint or OneDrive is an alternative Data leaks policy trigger.
claims.quote: DLP policy configured for High severity alerts (Exchange Online, SharePoint Online, or OneDrive for Business workloads only) OR Customized triggering indicators
